references.text: The immediate context where Moses asks to see God's glory, and God protects him by covering him with His hand.
Elijah stands in a cave on Mount Horeb (Sinai) as the Lord's glory passes by him, a parallel to Moses' experience in the cleft of the rock.
The Lord is described as a rock and a refuge, an image that connects to God protecting Moses in the rock.
God hides the believer in His shelter and lifts them up on a rock, paralleling how God placed Moses in the cleft of the rock.
Isaiah's vision of the Lord's glory in the temple, where God's majesty is revealed in an overwhelming way.
The Lord is described as an eternal rock, a refuge for believers.
The Word became flesh and we saw His glory (δόξαν), a fulfillment of the glory of God that Moses caught a glimpse of.
No one has ever seen God, but the Son has made Him known - connected to the fact that Moses could not see God's face fully.
Paul identifies the rock that followed Israel as Christ (ἡ πέτρα δὲ ἦν ὁ Χριστός), a typological connection to the rock where Moses was placed.
Both verses illustrate 'the Lord's hand' as an active force that physically leads and places the prophet in a meeting place with God's presence.
